claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit in the UK. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with a few basic questions:

1. **Do you have any children you're responsible for?** If yes, how many children are you asking about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. I'm asking about my son Alex - he's 8 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me ask you a few more questions to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. A few more questions:

**Are you the person primarily responsible for Alex's care?** In other words, do you provide for his needs such as food, clothes, and general upkeep?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am. I'm the one who takes care of him day-to-day - I provide his food, clothes, and everything he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, care, or any residential accommodation, or does he live with you full-time at home?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, he's been in hospital for a while now - about a couple of months or so. But I'm still his parent and responsible for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that. This is an important detail. I need to understand the situation a bit better:

**How many weeks has Alex been in hospital? Is it more or less than 12 weeks?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's been 11 weeks now, so just under 12 weeks.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. One more important question:

**During the time Alex has been in hospital, have you been regularly spending money on him?** This could include things like buying him clothes, toys, treats, or other items for his use.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have. I still buy his clothes, magazines, and his favorite food to bring to him at the hospital.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on the information you've provided:

- Alex is 8 years old (under 16) ✓
- You live in the UK ✓
- You are responsible for Alex's care and provide for his needs ✓
- Although Alex has been in hospital for 11 weeks, this is still under the 12-week threshold that could affect Child Benefit payments ✓
- You continue to regularly spend money on him (clothes, magazines, food), which demonstrates your ongoing financial responsibility ✓

You meet all the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit. Even if Alex's hospital stay extends beyond 12 weeks, you should still remain eligible because you're regularly spending money on him during his hospital stay - this is one of the exceptions to the 12-week rule.

If you haven't already claimed Child Benefit, you can apply. If you're already receiving it, you should continue to be entitled to it. However, you should inform HMRC about Alex's hospital stay so they have accurate information about your circumstances.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
